title: Lower six-month flow had no clear link to increased thermal sensitivity at 188 English river sites
abstract: We tested whether lower flow increased the annual temperature response of river family composition. We used 1,980 autumn samples at 188 English sites in 2001-2017, early-trained community directions from other sites, matched six-month flow quantiles, chemistry controls and site and year effects. The temperature-by-flow-deficit coefficient was -0.034, with a nominal 95% site-and-year cluster interval of -0.096 to 0.029. Lower flow was associated with warmer composition and more recorded families, but not clearly with greater annual family turnover in 1,633 consecutive-year pairs. Region-year effects, prior-year controls, a lower flow quantile and site resampling did not establish a positive interaction. Three-year time clusters gave a wider interval. These results do not support faster thermal response during the observed flow deficits. They do not rule out effects of severe drying. Air temperature, family-level recording, matched gauges, detection changes, selected sites, spatial benchmark confounding and incomplete joint uncertainty limit interpretation. The package includes code, aggregate results, figures, exact source hashes and an explicit dummy-regression audit. Raw data and record-level derivatives are excluded.
